parent.title: [{{date}}] Daily content pipeline
description: ## Daily Content Pipeline — {{date}}
Coordinate today's content production: 1 Dot by Dot article (tool guide, comparison, how-to). All departments are fair game. Quality over quantity.
## Your responsibilities
1. When SEO Expert finishes briefs: review them, assign a writing style (see below), then unblock the Copywriter task (set it to `todo`) posting the style parameters as a comment
2. When Copywriter finishes articles + PRs: unblock the Frontend Designer task (set it to `todo`)
3. When Designer finishes images: unblock the Legal Expert task (set it to `todo`)
4. When Legal approves: your merge task gets unblocked — do final review and merge
## Style assignment (do this in step 1, before unblocking Copywriter)

Read the Style Library at `/home/luca/paperclip/agents/superdots/style-library.md`. Check your memory key `recent_style_references` for the last 3-5 styles used. Select the style that best fits today's topic AND hasn't been used in the last 3 articles. Post the `## Style Parameters` block (style_reference, opening_hook, sentence_rhythm, pov, argument_structure, rationale) as a comment on the Copywriter task when setting it to `todo`. Update your memory with the new slug.
Subtasks track the individual steps.

tasks.title: [{{date}}] SEO brief: 1 high-quality article topic
description: ## Daily Content Pipeline — {{date}}
Research and provide a keyword-backed brief for 1 excellent blog article topic.
## Available data tools
- `node scripts/tools/gsc.mjs opportunities --json` — **START HERE**: queries where we have impressions but low CTR (quick wins for new content or refresh)
- `node scripts/tools/gsc.mjs queries --limit 30 --json` — what people actually search to find us (base briefs on REAL demand)
- `node scripts/tools/gsc.mjs pages --limit 20 --json` — our top performing pages (find gaps and related topics)
- `node scripts/tools/bing-webmaster.mjs query-stats --json` — same data from Bing (may reveal different keyword opportunities)
- `node scripts/tools/serpbear.mjs keywords superdots.sh --json` — tracked keyword rankings
- `node scripts/tools/seonaut.mjs summary --json` — latest SEO audit summary
- `node scripts/tools/searxng.mjs search "<keyword>" --json` — web search for competitor analysis, search intent
- `node scripts/tools/searxng.mjs top-results "<keyword>" --limit 5 --json` — top 5 SERP results with title, URL, snippet, position
- `node scripts/tools/searxng.mjs news "<topic>" --time week --json` — recent news for trending topics
## Key competitors to benchmark
zapier.com/blog, hubspot.com/blog, clickup.com/blog, notion.so/blog, jasper.ai/blog
## Strategic constraints (MANDATORY)
- **1 article per day only.** Quality over quantity. One excellent article beats three mediocre ones.
- **ONLY these departments**: Operations, Sales, Marketing. Do NOT brief articles for other departments until these 3 have deep coverage.
- **Keyword selection**: target long-tail keywords (4-5 words, 50-500 monthly volume, DR <30 in top 10). NO head terms we can't realistically rank for.
- **Conversion goal**: every article must include a natural newsletter CTA opportunity and internal links to the department's pillar page.
## Brief strategy

Prioritize topics based on GSC data: queries with high impressions but no existing article = content gap. Queries where we rank 8-20 = refresh candidate. Always cross-check with Bing data for additional opportunities.
## Step 1 — Competitor research (MANDATORY before writing brief)
Run `searxng.mjs top-results "<keyword>" --limit 5 --json` for the target keyword. Study the top 3 results:
- What angles do they cover?
- What's MISSING from their articles?
- What would make a reader prefer our version?
Include this analysis in the brief — the Copywriter needs it to write something genuinely different.
## Brief format
- **Target keyword** and search volume/difficulty estimate
- **Headline suggestion** — SEO-optimized and compelling
- **Content angle** — practical value for non-technical professionals
- **Suggested format** — one of: listicle, how-to guide, problem-solution, deep-dive, case-study
- **Differentiation angle** — SPECIFIC based on actual SERP results. What do the top 3 results miss? If you can't articulate what's different, pick a different keyword.
- **Competitor gap analysis** — what the top 3 articles cover vs what they lack
- **Required quality elements**: specific tool names with pricing, comparison table, 5+ FAQs, internal links to department pillar
- **Recommended structure** — headings, word count (min 2500), internal links
## Output
Post 1 brief as a comment on this task.
## When done
1. Set this task to `done`
2. @mention **@Content Manager** in a comment so they can review the briefs and unblock the Copywriter
## Deadline
Complete by 11:00 CET so the Content Manager can review before handing off to the Copywriter.

tasks.title: [{{date}}] Write articles and open PRs
description: ## Daily Content Pipeline — {{date}}
Write full articles based on article briefs from the Content Manager.
For each article:
1. Follow the **Git Publishing Procedure** in CLAUDE.md
2. Create branch `content/{{date}}_<slug>`
3. Write the article in `src/content/blog/<slug>.md`

4. Include an `imageHint` field in frontmatter — a short description (10-20 words) of what the hero image should depict, specific to the article content (e.g. `imageHint: "person at desk comparing two email drafts side by side"`)
5. Commit, push, open PR targeting `main`
6. Post the PR URL as a comment on this task
## Guidelines

- **Apply the assigned style**: read the `## Style Parameters` block in the SEO brief and apply it strictly. Open the Style Library at `/home/luca/paperclip/agents/superdots/style-library.md` to study the assigned writer's entry before writing.
- Write for busy professionals, not academics
- Every article MUST have a FAQ section (4-5 questions)
- One PR per article
- Use `node scripts/tools/searxng.mjs search "<topic>" --json` for fact-checking and competitor research
## When done
1. Set this task to `done`
2. @mention **@Content Manager** with all PR URLs so they can unblock the Designer
## Blocked on
Content Manager review of [{{seo_brief.identifier}}](/SUP/issues/{{seo_brief.identifier}}) SEO briefs.

tasks.title: [{{date}}] Generate AI hero images for new articles
description: ## Daily Content Pipeline — {{date}}
Generate AI hero images for today's new articles and push them to the Copywriter's open PRs.
## Steps
For each article PR opened by the Copywriter:
1. `git fetch origin && git checkout <branch-name> && git pull origin <branch-name>`
2. Run `node scripts/generate-ai-images.mjs --slug <article-slug>` to generate the hero image
3. Review the generated image against brand guidelines (see `scripts/image-style-config.json` qualityCalibration section). Regenerate if it doesn't meet standards.
4. Verify the image is specific to the article content, not generic. The article's `imageHint` frontmatter field describes what the image should depict.
5. Commit the image + updated frontmatter, push to the same branch
6. Comment on this task confirming images are done
## Requirements
- `REPLICATE_API_TOKEN` must be set (load from `.env`)
- Work on the **same branch** as the Copywriter's PR — do NOT create a new branch
- Check PR URLs in [{{write_articles.identifier}}](/SUP/issues/{{write_articles.identifier}}) task comments
## When done
1. Set this task to `done`
2. @mention **@Content Manager** confirming all images are pushed, so they can unblock Legal review
## Blocked on
Copywriter PRs from [{{write_articles.identifier}}](/SUP/issues/{{write_articles.identifier}}). Look for PR URLs in that task's comments.

tasks.title: [{{date}}] Legal compliance review of new articles
description: ## Daily Content Pipeline — {{date}}
Review today's article PRs for legal and compliance issues before publication.
## What to check
- GDPR compliance: no personal data collection claims without proper disclosure
- Affiliate/sponsorship disclosure if applicable
- No misleading claims about AI capabilities
- Copyright: no copied content, proper attribution
- Privacy policy consistency: if article references data handling, verify it matches our privacy policy
## Steps

For each article PR (find PR URLs in [{{hero_images.identifier}}](/SUP/issues/{{hero_images.identifier}}) and [{{write_articles.identifier}}](/SUP/issues/{{write_articles.identifier}}) task comments):
1. Read the article content in the PR branch
2. If **approved**: comment on this task "Approved: PR #XX" for each PR

3. If **changes needed**: create a new Paperclip task assigned to the relevant agent (Copywriter for content changes, Designer for image changes) with specific required fixes and a reference to the PR. Set this task to `blocked` until the fix task is done.
## When all PRs are approved
1. Set this task to `done`
2. @mention **@Content Manager** confirming legal approval so they can proceed with merge
## Blocked on
Images added to PRs by Frontend Designer [{{hero_images.identifier}}](/SUP/issues/{{hero_images.identifier}}).

tasks.title: [{{date}}] Final review and merge article PRs
description: ## Daily Content Pipeline — {{date}}
Final editorial review and merge of today's article PRs.
## Prerequisites
- All PRs have article content (Copywriter) + hero images (Designer)
- Legal review approved ([{{legal_review.identifier}}](/SUP/issues/{{legal_review.identifier}}))
## PILLAR CHECK (mandatory before merge)
Read the `contentPillar` field in each article's frontmatter.
- If `dot-by-dot`: proceed with merge after editorial checklist.
- If `connecting-the-dots`, `the-big-picture`, or `behind-the-dots`: **DO NOT MERGE.**
Create a new Paperclip task assigned to the CEO titled 'CEO approval needed: <article title>'
with the PR URL. Set this merge task to `blocked` until CEO approves.
The daily-content pipeline is for dot-by-dot articles only. Non-dot-by-dot articles
should come through the weekly-editorial-planning pipeline instead.
## Steps (for dot-by-dot articles)
For each article PR:
1. Final editorial quality check — apply the full 10-point checklist from your AGENTS.md
2. Verify hero image is present and appropriate
3. Verify CI passes
4. Merge PR to `main` using `gh pr merge <number> --merge --repo nio85/superdots-blog`
5. Verify deploy succeeded at https://superdots.sh
## After merging all PRs
1. Submit each new URL to IndexNow for instant search engine crawling:
`source .env && node scripts/tools/indexnow.mjs submit-url https://superdots.sh/blog/<slug>`
2. Comment on parent task [{{_parent.identifier}}](/SUP/issues/{{_parent.identifier}}) with published article URLs and IndexNow status. Close the parent task.
## Blocked on
Legal approval from [{{legal_review.identifier}}](/SUP/issues/{{legal_review.identifier}}).
